definition.statement: An AEM asset represents a single asset in the environment, unified (merged) and enriched with information from multiple sources, and the Assets page shows the sources and records it was merged from, its findings and its related tickets.

quotes: Each asset represents a single asset in your environment, unified (i.e., merged) and enriched with information from multiple sources.
view the sources and records from which it was merged, view the findings it contains, and view the tickets it's related to.

filters-and-discovery-action.statement: On the AEM Assets page assets can be filtered by Asset Is Crown Jewel, State, Owner ID or Source, grouped by fields such as Asset State, Asset ID or Asset Owner ID, and the EASM discovery profile can be configured from the page.

quotes: Filter assets by Asset Is Crown Jewel, State, Owner ID, or Source.
Group assets by fields such as Asset State, Asset ID, or Asset Owner ID.
Configure the EASM discovery profile to scan and monitor your external attack surface.

charts.statement: The Assets overview charts show assets by risk score in increments of 0.5 (X-axis the max severity score of active findings), and the 5 most frequent asset types and operating systems.

quotes: Displays the number of assets in the different risk score ranges (in increments of 0.5).
The X-axis represents the max severity score of active findings related to the asset, and the colors represent the risk category.
Presents the asset count categorized by asset type, displaying the 5 most frequently occurring types.
Displays the number of assets categorized by operating system, displaying the 5 most frequently occurring types.

risk-score-mass.statement: With the default Active saved view, an asset's Risk Score is initially set by the default reconciliation function and reflects the highest severity score among its findings (customizable through Data Unification), and Risk Mass is the sum of the severity scores of its active findings.

quotes: When the default Active saved view is selected, you can see the following details for each asset:
The risk score is initially set by the default reconciliation function, and reflects the highest severity score among the findings. The default can be customized through Data Unification.
Risk Mass: The sum of all severity scores of the active findings associated with the asset.

crown-jewel-seen.statement: Is Crown Jewel is a TRUE/FALSE field for whether the asset is one of the most valuable assets; First Seen is the earliest date a finding on the asset was first detected, Last Seen the latest date a finding was detected, and Total Findings the sum of active findings per severity.

quotes: Is Crown Jewel: A boolean field with values of TRUE or FALSE indicating whether the asset is defined as a crown jewel asset
(i.e., one of your organization's most valuable assets)
First Seen: The earliest date on which a finding on the asset was first detected.
Last Seen: The latest date on which a finding on the asset was detected.
Total Findings: The sum of the active findings per severity.

drawer.statement: The actions in the asset drawer depend on the user role in AEM, the drawer can be configured by admins so it may look different in an account, and the drawer opens with a Top Panel and tabs including Asset Merging and Findings.

quotes: The actions you can perform in the asset drawer depend on your user role in AEM.
The asset drawer can be configured by admins and might look different in your account.

system-views.title: Which system-saved views the Assets page offers
system-views.detail: The Assets page lists its system-saved views in a collapsed list that is absent from the capture; only the default Active view is named.

drawer-tabs.title: What the asset drawer tabs contain
drawer-tabs.detail: The drawer page names its Top Panel, Details, Asset Merging, Findings and Tickets sections but shows only an image placeholder; the fields in each are not captured.
